text: will you log how much data is being transfered when loading the app, because it should be megabytes not hundreds but tens
resolution: User wants to see how much data crosses to the host on app load (expects tens of MB, suspects hundreds). Added a [flush-bytes] meter in renderer/hostConfig.ts at the real transport boundary (flushCoalesced → transportFlush): a cumulative g_totalFlushBytes counter that logs '+XKB → total YMB (#N, M cmd)' per non-trivial flush (>4KB), with a per-op byte breakdown (CREATE/UPDATE/… = count/KB) for fat flushes (>64KB) so the bloated command type is named. Tiny per-frame UPDATE batches (<4KB) are skipped to avoid steady-state spam. Hot-reloadable (bundled into the cart); left uncommitted alongside the other [propgone]/[flush] diagnostics on the dirty tree. Awaiting the user's startup log — the plateau total answers tens-vs-hundreds and the breakdown surfaces whether CREATE commands hauling mesh verts/instance arrays/atlases are the weight (and tests the ~512MB-flush suspicion with real numbers).
